prediction.likelyOutcome: JMR is well positioned to prevail on liability against EAR (and derivatively SureTec) given consistent percipient-witness testimony and a reasoned expert delay/cost allocation, but the modified-total-cost drywall claim and the Eichleay claim both carry real methodological risk that will trim recovery below the pleaded ceiling. EAR will likely recover some or most of its retention, substantially offset against JMR's proven delay damages, producing a net recovery for JMR materially below the sum of its raw claimed figures.

outcome.description: After a five-day bench trial (January 2012) the court found for JMR and, after JMR withdrew one claim and adjusted another in its proposed statement of decision, entered judgment on August 14, 2012 for a net $315,631: $29,249 air compressor, $132,168 field overhead for delay, $15,440 field overhead for closeout, $14,244 markup, $60,693 Eichleay home office overhead and $185,730 framing/drywall disruption, less $121,893 retention withheld; EAR took nothing on its cross-complaint. A later order awarded JMR $90,644.07 in section 998 expert fees and found it entitled to attorney fees (amount undetermined) for defending the cross-complaint. On December 30, 2015 the Sixth District affirmed the judgment (Eichleay and modified total cost methods upheld, surety liable) and reversed the expert-fee award as premature.
outcome.attorneysFeesOnAppeal: entitlement to fees for defending the cross-complaint found but amount never fixed; $90,644.07 expert-fee award reversed
outcome.finalNote: Judgment affirmed; expert-fee order reversed and remanded.
